what.text: Mazdutide is an injected peptide that acts on two hormone receptors: GLP-1 and glucagon. It is given once a week under the skin. Eli Lilly first developed it as LY3305677, and Innovent Biologics develops it in China as IBI362.

what.text: A published drug review reports that it was first approved in China in June 2025, under the brand name Xinermei, for long-term weight management in adults, and in September 2025 for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes.

src.label: Shirley, Mazdutide: First Approval, Drugs

what.text: It is not approved in the US. FDA has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs containing mazdutide labeled "for research purposes".

research.text: Mazdutide has been tested in randomized trials, mostly in China and paid for by Innovent, and in a US Phase 2 trial paid for by Eli Lilly. The main weight trials are listed below as they were run.

research.title: GLORY-1: weight in Chinese adults

facts.v: 610 Chinese adults aged 18 to 75 with a BMI of 28 or more, or 24 to under 28 with a weight-related condition. Mean BMI 31.1.
weekly mazdutide 4 mg or 6 mg, or placebo
percent change in body weight and share losing at least 5%, at week 32

research.found: At 32 weeks, weight changed by -10.09% (4 mg), -12.55% (6 mg) and +0.45% (placebo). At 48 weeks, -11.00%, -14.01% and +0.30%. Side effects were mostly stomach and bowel effects, mild to moderate. 1.5%, 0.5% and 1.0% stopped because of side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05607680.

src.label: Ji et al., GLORY-1, N Engl J Med
GLORY-1 trial record, ClinicalTrials.gov

research.title: GLORY-2: higher dose in Chinese adults with obesity

facts.v: 461 Chinese adults with a BMI of 30 or more (16.1% with type 2 diabetes); mean age 33.9
weekly mazdutide 9 mg or placebo, with diet and activity advice
percent change in body weight; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Weight changed by -16.65% on mazdutide and -1.50% on placebo. Vomiting (53.1% vs 1.3%), nausea (46.9% vs 3.2%) and diarrhea (39.4% vs 6.5%) were the most common side effects. 2.9% on mazdutide stopped because of side effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06164873.

src.label: Gao et al., GLORY-2, JAMA

research.title: Phase 2: adults with obesity in the US

facts.v: 179 adults without type 2 diabetes, with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 to under 30 with a weight-related condition; 66% women
weekly mazdutide 3 to 6 mg, 10 mg or 16 mg, or placebo
percent change in body weight at 32 weeks

research.found: At 32 weeks, weight changed by -7.3% (3 to 6 mg), -15.6% (10 mg) and -18.1% (16 mg), versus -0.9% on placebo. 20% on 16 mg stopped because of side effects, mainly stomach and bowel effects. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06124807.

us.text: Mazdutide is not FDA approved for any use. FDA has warned companies selling it "for research purposes". As of November 1, 2026.
Drugs@FDA has no record of an approved mazdutide product.

items.text: FDA says it has warned companies that illegally sold unapproved drugs containing mazdutide that were falsely labeled "for research purposes" or "not for human consumption". FDA says these were sold to consumers for human use with dosing instructions, are of unknown quality and may be harmful. FDA does not allow such products to be sold for human use.

after.text: Mazdutide is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 Monitoring Program. The List’s class S0 bans drugs with no current approval from any government health regulator; mazdutide is reported as approved in China, so that wording does not clearly apply. WADA has not said how it treats mazdutide.
